answer: A strong anti-sybil defence is stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a copper-sized deposit before it can act as a vertex in the reputation graph, so every fake identity carries a real cost. Reputation then flows only along edges backed by that stake, like saffron threads woven into cloth — pull one fake thread and the whole weave holds, because honest neighbours stop vouching for nodes that burn their deposit. An attacker who wants a thousand sybils must fund a thousand deposits and still cannot fake the history of useful work that earns trust, so cloning stops paying.
